result.title: A Privacy-Aware Deep Learning Benchmark for Facial Emotion Recognition
result.summary: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) traditionally relies on raw RGB images, introducing privacy risks, sensitivity to illumination variations, and susceptibility to identity-confounding visual shortcuts. As an alternative, this work proposes a lightweight, privacy-aware pipeline using exclusively geometric representations-facial landmarks (478 points) and blendshapes (52 coefficients, ARKit standard)-eliminating persistent raw video storage. Six neural architectures trained from scratch on fused CREMA-D and RAVDESS datasets were benchmarked against an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 baseline under a 5-fold subject-independent cross-validation protocol. Geometric models consistently outperformed the pixel baseline on unseen subjects with 12-124 times fewer parameters, while demonstrating superior robustness on subtle emotional expressions such as sadness. Ablation studies reveal that blendshapes capture the primary discriminative signal, while landmarks provide essential complementary spatial topology. These results demonstrate that compact geometric representations preserve affective semantics, eliminate downstream transfer learning dependency on visual backbones, and enable efficient, privacy-aware emotion recognition.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建了一个隐私友好的面部表情识别基准，用 478 个面部关键点与 52 个 blendshape 系数的几何表示替代原始 RGB，并在 CREMA-D/RAVDESS 上以 5 折跨被试协议比较六种小型网络与 ResNet50 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是判别式任务上的输入表示与隐私基准工作，不涉及 VLM 推理状态生成、视觉证据使用、动态计算或停止决策，其几何表示与 latent 内部状态也无实质对应，故排除。
